assets.description: A simplified landscape with a flowing river, a lake beside trees, droplets on a leaf, and water shown below the ground.
Three panels show solid ice, liquid water in a glass, and symbolic dots for invisible water vapor. The dots are representations, not visible vapor.
A left-to-right arrow labeled melting connects ice to liquid water; a right-to-left arrow labeled freezing connects liquid water to ice.
The same puddle is larger earlier and smaller later. Dotted upward arrows represent invisible water vapor leaving the liquid surface; runoff and infiltration are excluded.
A cold glass has liquid drops on the outside. Dashed arrows from the surrounding air indicate water vapor moving toward the cold surface, not water passing through the glass.
A simplified cloud contains small water droplets and ice symbols. Larger drops fall downward as rain; this shows one simplified precipitation route.
A simplified water cycle shows evaporation upward from a lake, condensation in clouds, rain downward, and surface water flowing back to the lake. Other routes are omitted.
A new scene shows a wet cloth on a line, a puddle on the ground, and droplets outside a cold glass on a table. Dashed arrows symbolize invisible water vapor.
Atmospheric paper-cut and gouache landscape cover for Water and Weather; decorative course artwork, separate from the scientific diagrams.
